question.text: Adequate disclosure of derivative activities in financial statements must include:

answer.text: Accounting policies, risk management objectives, and hedging activities
Only gains and losses for the year

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the ETIRD workbook (p.297), adequate disclosures in financial statements must cover accounting policies, risk management objectives, and hedging activities related to derivatives. This gives stakeholders the information needed to assess the entity's derivative exposure. The Trap: Notional amounts alone are insufficient — they don't indicate the actual risk. Reporting only P&L misses the risk management context. Disclosing only counterparties is not the prescribed scope. Note: Limit disclosures to the source-backed scope: accounting policies, risk management objectives, and hedging activities, as stated on page 297.
